chunks: And Talakbari narrated this report, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Nahwandi, from Al-Hasan ibn Ja'far ibn Muslim Al-Hanafi, from Abu Hamid Al-Muraghi, who said:
I asked Hakima bint Muhammad, the sister of Abu Al- Hasan Al-Askari… and he narrated like it.

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْعَسْكَرِيُّ: Abu Al-Hasan Al- Askari, referring to Imam Hasan al-Askari (AS)
key_terms.التَّلْعَكْبَرِيُّ: Talakbari, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.النَّهَوَنْدِيِّ: Al-Nahwandi, a nisba indicating origin from Nahavand
key_terms.الْحَنَفِيِّ: Al-Hanafi, a nisba indicating affiliation with the Hanafah tribe
key_terms.حَكِيمَةَ بِنْتَ مُحَمَّدٍ: Hakima bint Muhammad, a prominent female narrator and sister of the Imams

ai.seo_question: Who did Abu Hamid Al-Muraghi ask for information regarding the Imam?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes a crucial link in the chain of evidence for the birth of Imam al-Mahdi (aj) through Hakima bint Muhammad, the sister of Imam al-Askari, thereby validating the testimony of the Ahl al-Bayt during the Minor and Major Ghaiba. It underscores the scholarly tradition of relying on female members of the Imams' households as authoritative transmitters of esoteric knowledge and historical facts regarding the twelfth Imam's lineage.
